rfm_tuples.f: Parse Form 4 XML for code-P (open-market purchases) by named executives/directors across the 18 months preceding the 2026-05-25 cutoff (2024-11-26 to 2026-05-25). Count buys vs sells and characterize timing.
rfm_tuples.M_value: ZERO code-P open-market purchases by any insider over 18 months pre-cutoff. 72 Form 4 filings parsed, 90 non-derivative transactions: 41 code-F (tax withholding on RSU vest), 35 code-A (RSU/PSU grants at $0), 11 code-S (open-market sales), 2 code-G (gifts), 1 code-D (disposition). The asymmetric absence — particularly post-Feb 2026 10-K, post-Apr 30 Q1 print, post-May 19 UK leadership shuffle — is itself the signal. Code-A grants and code-F withholdings are mechanical and provide no information; the absence of code-P provides strong negative information.

Specifically: (a) CFO Daniel McHenry sold 6,000 shares across 7 lots on 2025-06-11 at $440.99-$445.94 for ~$2.65M total — this is BETWEEN Q1 2025 earnings (Apr 24) and the Q2 release (Aug 5) when FY2025 numbers were not yet public; (b) SVP Aftersales Michael Jones sold 1,613 sh on 2025-04-30 at $405.57 ($654K) — the same day as the Q1 2025 earnings 8-K; (c) Pereira Lincoln sold 7,000 sh on 2025-08-27 at $469.33 ($3.29M) — the LAST sale in the dataset, two weeks after Q2 2025 8-K and within ~6 weeks of the 9/2/2025 JLR cybersecurity incident that became a material headwind (JLR = 3.6% of FY2025 revenue); (d) Pereira also sold 6,000 sh on 2024-12-18 at $426.68 ($2.56M) just before FY2024 10-K. Aggregate code-S proceeds $9.37M, all between $405-$469 per share. ZERO code-P purchases when the stock then fell to ~$320 area at cutoff. P:S ratio = 0.00x.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B finding: the timing pattern is exactly what 'informed insider selling' looks like — concentrated near the highs, by the CFO and an SVP, ahead of revenue/earnings deceleration that the issuer subsequently disclosed. The CFO single-day sale of $2.65M on 2025-06-11 is particularly notable because no 10b5-1 plan was disclosed as active in the Q4 2025 disclosure window (per 10-K Item 9B: 'no director or officer... adopted or terminated a Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement' Q4 2025). The asymmetric sell:buy ratio of infinity into a -33% drawdown is one of the strongest Signal-OS bearish primitives.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Item 1 strategy framing: 'Our diversified portfolio, balanced capital allocation framework, and adjusted leverage provide flexibility to pursue acquisitions while continuing to return capital to stockholders through share repurchases and dividends.'

rfm_tuples.M_value: Diluted EPS continuing-ops: 2023 $42.75 → 2024 $36.72 (-14%) → 2025 $25.13 (-32%). Two consecutive years of double-digit EPS decline, -41% peak-to-2025. Income from operations: 2023 $968.6M → 2024 $909.1M → 2025 $734.0M (-19% YoY, -24% from 2023). Net income: 2023 $601.6M → 2024 $498.1M → 2025 $325.2M (-46% from peak). rfm_tuples.interpretation: Issuer discloses the numbers cleanly in the financial statements — no GAAP manipulation. But the gap between the upbeat strategic narrative ('flexibility', 'consistent return-based framework') and the underlying -41% EPS decline over two years is large. The drawdown is rationalized by these honest disclosures, not unfair-market action.

rfm_tuples.f: Decompose the Q1 print into organic vs financial-engineering drivers (revenue, gross profit, operating income, gain on disposals, share count).

rfm_tuples.R: Deloitte CAM (10-K, p.50-51): 'We identified the U.K. reporting unit goodwill impairment assessments as a critical audit matter because of the significant judgments made by management to estimate the fair value including revenue growth rates, future EBITDA margins, the WACC, and market multiples.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — given the CAM call-out, verify whether the UK operational/regulatory backdrop supports management's go-forward UK EBITDA assumptions.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors UK section + Note 12 + Q1 10-Q UK segment + restructuring notes)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Three independent UK headwinds disclosed: (1) JLR cybersecurity incident Sept 2, 2025 — JLR = 3.6% of consolidated FY2025 revenues — 'the temporary shutdown of certain production facilities' and 'delays in new vehicle deliveries, reduced availability'; (2) UK BEV mandate ('battery electric vehicle mandates in the U.K. and their impact on new vehicle demand'); (3) 'agency model' adoption by certain OEMs reducing UK-reported revenue. Operational evidence: (a) 2024 Restructuring Plan ($16.7M) + 2025 Restructuring Plan ($28.4M) both targeting the UK segment for cost reduction post-Inchcape integration; (b) UK fixed-asset impairments $7.4M in FY2025 (vs zero in FY2024); (c) Total FY2025 asset impairments $192.8M = 5.8x FY2024 ($33.0M); (d) On 2026-05-19, the UK CEO Mark Raban was replaced by US-CFO McHenry as new UK President & CEO (8-K 5/21) — a senior-leadership change at the impaired segment immediately before cutoff. Goodwill on the balance sheet declined from $2,204.9M (YE25) to $2,126.5M (Q1 2026), suggesting Q1 goodwill activity (impairment or held-for-sale reclass) of ~$78M.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The UK reporting unit is the explicit auditor concern, and Mode-B evidence shows three concurrent stresses (cyber-disrupted top OEM, regulatory BEV-mandate demand drag, leadership change). The May-19 management swap of the US CFO into the UK President role is a strong implied signal that the UK segment needed direct US-leadership intervention. This raises the probability that another UK goodwill impairment is taken in FY2026 — exactly the risk the CAM was written to highlight.

rfm_tuples.R: 8-K 2026-03-03 Item 5.02: 'On March 2, 2026, Group 1 Automotive... and Mr. Daryl Kenningham entered into a second amendment... which restructures the severance benefits payable upon certain qualifying termination events.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — verify what the amendment actually does (enhance vs reduce severance) and whether the timing relative to the drawdown matters.
rfm_tuples.M_value: The amendment ADDS Corporate Change protection: 1.5x base+target bonus + 18 months COBRA on Constructive Termination / Without-Cause / company breach; ESCALATING to 2.0x + 24 months COBRA if termination is within six months of a Corporate Change. It also adds COBRA for the first time and prorates the annual bonus. The amendment was executed 3 weeks after the FY2025 10-K disclosed -32% EPS decline, with the stock already meaningfully off its highs. No countervailing claw-back or holdback was added.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: CEO severance enhancement in the middle of a deep drawdown, with Corporate-Change protection language explicitly inserted, is a soft signal that the board is hedging against (i) potential CEO departure under pressure or (ii) M&A optionality on the corporate level. Not red-flag fraud, but the 'why now' question is governance-relevant. Combined with the UK-leadership shuffle two months later, it suggests management/board are preparing the chair for turbulence.

summary: GPI is a -33% drawdown name where the Form-4 forensic tape is the OPPOSITE of peer ABG and aligns strongly with the bear case. ZERO open-market purchases by ANY insider over 18 months despite the deep drawdown, $378.7M open buyback authorization, and management's externally-stated 'sufficient liquidity' narrative. Instead, the historical insider tape is clustered SELLING near the 2025 highs: CFO Daniel McHenry sold $2.65M on 2025-06-11 at $440-446, director Pereira sold $5.85M across two windows ending 2025-08-27 at $469 — two weeks before the JLR cyber incident (JLR = 3.6% of revenue) was publicly disclosed. P:S ratio = 0.00x with infinite asymmetry. The recent 2026-05-19 8-K shows the US CFO McHenry being moved into the UK President/CEO role — exactly the segment that Deloitte flagged as a critical audit matter for goodwill impairment, and where two restructuring plans ($16.7M + $28.4M) and a $7.4M UK fixed-asset impairment have already been recognized. CEO Kenningham's severance was simultaneously enhanced (Corp Change protection added March 2, 2026). Fundamentals: FY2025 EPS -32% YoY (-41% two-year), asset impairments +485% YoY, Q1 2026 revenue -1.8% (first quarterly decline), operating cash flow -42%, and the EPS 'beat' is fully explained by buybacks shrinking shares -9% plus a $48M disposition gain. Liquidity and covenants are intact (clean Deloitte opinion, $589M debt paydown in Q1) so this is NOT a balance-sheet collapse — but the forensic insider behavior, the UK CAM exposure, and the masked organic decline produce a SHORT-tier verdict. Severity: 1 PASS / 0 UNVERIFIABLE / 5 MODERATE / 2 SEVERE / 1 RED_FLAG.
